chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi, said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, Hisham ibn Udayn asked me to ask you about a man who designated the emancipation of his slave to take effect upon the occurrence of death by his master. So the master died, and upon him was an obligatory freeing of a neck as an expiation. Is the emancipation of that slave, which the master had designated for him, valid on behalf of the deceased for the freeing of the neck that was upon the deceased?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

key_terms.كَفَّارَةٍ: Expiation (penalty for a specific act or vow)

ai.seo_question: Does the emancipation of a slave designated for after-death take effect as an obligatory expiation for the deceased master?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a slave manumitted via a master's bequest (mukatab or conditional itq) after death does not fulfill the specific obligation of freeing a slave for expiation (kaffarah). This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that the legal nature of the emancipation—whether it is a gift, a bequest, or a direct expiation—determines its validity for specific religious duties, ensuring the expiation is performed with the requisite intentionality and immediacy.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Hisham Bin Adeyn asked me to ask you<sup>asws</sup> about a man who made the emancipation of his slave if there were to occur the event of death with his master. So the master died, and upon him was an Obligatory emancipation of a neck with regards to an expiation. Is it allowed, on behalf of the deceased, an emancipation of the slave for whom the master had made the emancipation to be for him, after his death, in the freeing of the neck which was upon the deceased?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
